1850.note: The only cipher items in Mazarine Ms 4376 are no. 78 'Affaire de madame du Fargis et ses lettres' (f. 301) and three name keys dated March 1650 (nos. 79-81, ff. 334-338). The Du Fargis letters and the Chemerault letters with their name-code 'jargon' key were printed in 1650 in the 'Journal de M. le Cardinal duc de Richelieu' (pp. 97-119 for Du Fargis). Dubuisson-Aubenay's copies are very probably taken from that print or its source, so the texts were read and keyed in print. Medium confidence: the copies were not seen.

2926.note: HMC Portland VIII (1907) pp. 234-235 gives the editor's own description: 'eleven small folios of cypher in numbers', filed after Blencowe's letter of 22 Jun 1706 in which the government decipherer says he 'advanced not one step'. No reading is printed or noted. Low confidence because the volume of the Harley papers holding the folios is not identified. The editor only guesses ('perhaps') that they are the letters Blencowe failed on, and they sit beside Bobin's keys, which could read them.

2724.note: The Birago letters are in fr. 3251 and 3252, not fr. 3231/3232. Tomokiyo's Cryptiana page nevers.htm catalogues every fr. 3251 Birago cipher letter. Only no. 63 (f. 119, numerical) is 'not deciphered', and it is already the repository target 'birago'. Lasry read fr. 3252 no. 24 in part with the Ceppo-Nevers key (target birago1571). The rest is a key lookup with published keys, not an open problem; no. 63 stays with its own target.
